So far so good - After the original ice maker called it quits, I had two choices: call the service or do something about it myself. A service call in my area is $150 just for a technician to come in and say "hello", and then I pay extra for any parts he has to install... So this would have been at least a $200 job. Compared to $40 (at the time of my purchase) and a 5 minutes to replace (tip - use a mirror to see the screws and work on them) - even if it fails within a few months and I have to buy another one, It's still going to worth it financially. In fact, simple math suggests, that I'd have to go through five of these before I begin losing money compared to a service call.

I'll rate installation difficulty 2 out of 5, but only because you have to use a socket screwdriver, which may not be available at every home, and work on the screws that are out of your direct view. Otherwise it is a very simple job. It was said in many reviews, and I am going to repeat it just in case: do not completely remove the screws. Just loosen them, and slide your old contraption up and out. There are lots of YouTube videos showing exactly how it's done.

Terrible Overpriced Product - MyPod is MUCH better - Save yourself a Save yourself a lot of time. . . hassle. . . and money. Do a search for MyPod.

First, Ecopad's are expensive! Even if you can find them for $5.00, it's too much money. (MyPod is currently under $10.00, very durable and easy) MyPod is also currently being sold through Amazon.com so if you purchase more than $25.00, or if you're a "Prime" member, you get free shipping!

Second, they are a BIG hassle. If you don't have a grinder, then you have to find a place to find the beans fine. It's very time consuming putting the grounds in the holder and packing them in. It's also messy. If you don't put enough ground in, then you're going to have a weak cup of coffee. If you pack too much in, the thing will crack or the screens rupture. Heaven help you if you don't have the top completely sealed. Also, you can't make cup after cup because you have to clean the Ecopad out and make sure it's completely dry before filling again. None of this is true with MyPod. You use drip-grind coffee, it's easy to fill/refill, it's very durable.

Though nothing will ever be as simple as purchasing Senseo Coffee Pods, I must say that there's really not one thing I like about Ecopad, and there's lots to like about MyPod. Don't get me wrong, MyPod isn't perfect, but it's certainly much. . . Much. . . MUCH better than Ecopad.

Knobs not compatible with original Jenn-Air KIP-5D09-3/-4/-1 knobs - The knobs sold on Amazon looked almost identical to the ones on my 2003 Jenn Air stove, so I assumed they would fit. They didn't. The original Jenn Air stove knobs have the ID letters/numbers "KIP-5D09-3", or -4, or -1 as the final number on the inside of the knob. The REPLACEMENT knobs have the ID letters/numbers "KIP-5D01-2", or -3 as the final number. Note the originals knobs are 5D09 (NINE!!) and replacements are 5D01 (ONE!) which are a tad too small and do not fit my Jenn Air stove. Therefore, be certain to pre-check the numbers on your knobs to determine if your stove requires the 5D09's OR the 5D01's. Thank you.

The design changed so these no longer fit as designed, I made it work though. - Bosch changed the design of how the tab at the end of this cord connects to the spring which regulates the soft opening of the dishwasher door (our dishwasher is 5-6 years old). This tab doesn't insert into the original plastic clip on the spring, buyer beware. In the end I removed the plastic clip from the spring and simply threaded the new cord through the coils of the spring and used the plastic tab on the end of the cord to act as a stop from pulling through the coil. The tension of the spring coils keeps the tab locked inside the barrel of the spring. For now this solution works, the tension is a bit too tight and I imagine after many uses the spring will "saw" though the cord but after spending all the time pulling out my dishwasher to discover this part is no longer correct I decided to make it work and I did. If you use "coarse of medium" grind, your coffee will be very weak as they are very granulated and the machine won't have enough time to infuse and remove the coffee flavor from it. Does its job if you keep an eye on it - I purchased this unit 6 months ago. I vented the unit outside using a very short, straight vent. The dryer does work for small loads, but does not dry large loads well most likely due to the lint trap. In fact, the lint trap seems to be holding the unit back from doing a better job all around.

I find with medium sized loads I need to clean the lint trap multiple times to dry well. This would be fine except that it is difficult to access the lint trap with any clothes in the dryer. Even without clothes, the lint trap is circular and presses against the rear of the barrel which makes it slightly difficult to access, remove, and replace. My fiance and I have found one of the lint trap filters rolling around with the rest of the laundry more than once (due to it falling off while trying to replace it).

Cleaning the lint trap can also be a chore. The manual suggest lint-brushing/vacuuming the filter which works if the filter doesn't get sucked into the vacuum as well.

The unit works better than air-drying and is exactly what I needed in my apartment. The lint trap/filer could certainly use improved access. The fact that I can plug it into a regular wall outlet is great. Make sure to turn other electronics off on the same circuit though.

I would purchase this unit again since I don't have special electric/gas hookups or perm. venting options in my apartment.

I replaced the icemaker because it overfilled by a teaspoon of water on each refill, spilling into the ice drawer and down the inside of the freezer compartment onto the frozen food. Once a month I'd have to empty the freezer, chipping the ice that had accumulated on the freezer wall and the food. After trying the suggestions on the LG website, I gave up and replaced the unit and the new icemaker works great. A larger lip has been added around the top of the ice cube tray on the new icemaker that contains the water as it flows into the end of the tray giving it time to flow into the other end of the tray as the level equalizes. Had I recognized the modification on the new icemaker before installing it, I might have been able to make that modification to my old icemaker instead of spending the $120 on the new one. Other than that overflow issue caused by a design error, the old icemaker still worked great.
